facts: Ordnance Survey mapping cannot replicate the exact position of every physical feature on the ground.
Variation between real-world position and mapped position is described as specified accuracy tolerance.
Distances scaled between mapped features may not exactly match distances measured on the ground.
Mapping accuracy varies with map scale and the original survey method.
A line on a 1:1250 map roughly represents 0.3m on the ground.
A line on a 1:2500 map roughly represents 0.6m on the ground.
guards: Do not infer sub-0.3m positional certainty from a 1:1250 mapped line alone.
Do not infer sub-0.6m positional certainty from a 1:2500 mapped line alone.
Do not treat scaled map distance as surveyed ground distance.
Keep map scale, survey accuracy and legal-boundary certainty as separate fields.
Reject any workflow that converts line width directly into an exact legal boundary.
Require stronger boundary evidence before pairing map-only geometry with centimetre-level elevation claims.

facts: Most registered boundaries are subject to the general boundaries rule.
The general-boundary red line has a zone of uncertainty rather than exact legal-line precision.
A determined boundary is different because it records the exact line after that line has been identified.
The legal boundary depends on the relevant conveyance or transfer as a whole, including its plan.
Where a plan is unclear, extrinsic evidence and physical features existing at the relevant time may be considered.
Even precise physical features can be difficult to re-identify later if the feature changes or disappears.
guards: Do not promote ordinary red edging to exact legal geometry.
Do not substitute current physical occupation for historic legal-boundary evidence without provenance.
Keep determined-boundary evidence distinct from general-boundary evidence.
Quarantine candidates where deed/transfer evidence conflicts with mapped or current physical features.
Do not attach centimetre-level elevation differences to a boundary whose horizontal legal position is unresolved.
Require evidence hierarchy and date context to be recorded before exact-boundary sampling.

facts: The Environment Agency Time Stamped DTM catalogue was updated on 7 April 2026.
Site-specific LIDAR surveys have been carried out across England since 1998.
Available raster resolutions include 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m depending on the survey.
The DTM removes surface objects to represent terrain surface.
Downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files aligned to the OS Grid and referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The stated vertical accuracy is +/-15cm RMSE.
guards: Require the actual survey resolution for each parcel sample rather than assuming 1m.
Require survey date and tile provenance before treating a DTM value as temporally specific.
Do not mix Newlyn-referenced heights with another vertical datum without explicit transformation.
Do not report raster cell size as vertical accuracy.
Carry the +/-15cm RMSE source-accuracy statement separately from stored numeric precision.
Reject candidate promotion when the required 5km tile provenance cannot be reconstructed.

facts: Time Stamped DSM data is available at 25cm, 50cm, 1m and 2m resolutions depending on survey requirements.
DSM values include terrain plus objects such as vehicles, buildings and vegetation.
DSM downloads are GeoTIFF rasters in 5km zip files aligned to the OS Grid.
DSM elevations are referenced to Ordnance Survey Newlyn.
The stated vertical accuracy is +/-15cm RMSE.
Coverage metadata provides survey dates, resolution, transformation and geoidal-model information for a location.
guards: Do not substitute DSM for bare-earth DTM in a ground-height-difference metric.
Require coverage metadata before assuming the transformation used by a historical survey.
Do not assume two DSM/DTM tiles share an acquisition date without metadata confirmation.
Flag buildings, vehicles and vegetation as possible DSM surface contamination.
Do not merge different survey resolutions without recording resampling provenance.
Require explicit surface semantics whenever DSM is used for a non-ground analytical purpose.

facts: Environment Agency point-cloud data is available for surveys going back to 2006.
A matching point cloud does not necessarily exist for every historic DTM or DSM because of archive history.
Point-cloud returns are classified into ground and surface-object classes during processing.
Manual editing of the derived DTM means classified ground points may not match the final DTM exactly.
Point clouds are supplied as LAZ files in 5km download zip files aligned to the OS grid.
Coverage metadata includes survey flight dates and average point density where available.
guards: Do not claim point-cloud verification when no matching survey cloud is documented.
Do not treat classified ground points as identical to the final edited DTM.
Require survey-date matching before comparing point cloud and raster samples.
Record average point density when using point cloud as supporting evidence.
Keep raw-point classification provenance separate from derived-raster provenance.
Reject a cross-check if the LAZ tile and raster tile cannot be tied to the same location and survey context.

facts: OS Terrain 5 grid data uses regular 5m post spacing.
The product is supplied in 5km by 5km tiles.
Each grid height represents the mean height across the whole 5m pixel.
The ASCII grid represents the value at the pixel centre, 2.5m from the pixel edge.
Height values are stored to the nearest 0.01m.
Tile metadata includes information such as the flying date and CRS is EPSG:27700.
guards: Do not interpret 0.01m storage precision as centimetre-level measurement accuracy.
Do not treat the 5m pixel mean as an exact point elevation at a parcel vertex.
Use pixel-centre/grid semantics consistently when sampling or interpolating.
Require tile flying-date metadata when temporal comparability matters.
Reject CRS-implicit sampling; EPSG:27700 handling must be explicit.
Do not compare a raster-cell mean with a point-cloud return without describing the aggregation difference.

facts: OS Terrain 5 is a mid-resolution DTM with 5m post spacing and 5m interval contours.
The current product page describes typical accuracy as greater than 2m RMSE.
Published sample-area RMSE values are 1.5m for urban/major communication routes and 2.5m for rural and mountain/moorland areas.
OS Terrain 5 documentation states the product is updated quarterly in January, April, July and October.
Grid and contour products are based on the same source data.
Whole-tile refreshes regenerate sequential feature identifiers for the release.
guards: Do not use OS Terrain 5 as a centimetre-accuracy acceptance source.
Record the applicable terrain-context RMSE when using Terrain 5 as fallback evidence.
Do not treat a feature identifier as stable across tile refreshes.
Capture release/tile provenance for repeatable cross-checks.
Prefer higher-resolution official LiDAR where available for parcel-scale ground-height sampling.
Do not combine quarterly Terrain 5 data with time-stamped LiDAR as if acquisition dates were identical.

facts: OSTN15 is the definitive OSGB36/ETRS89 transformation used with OS Net.
OSTN15 with OS Net station coordinates defines the National Grid rather than the old triangulation network.
Refixed and archived OSGB36 positions can differ, although they agree on average to better than about 0.1m RMSE.
OSGB36 and ODN remain the basis of OS mapping for the foreseeable future.
OSTN15 and OSGM15 provide access from ETRS89 GNSS coordinates to OSGB36 and the appropriate height datum.
The transformation workflow must distinguish horizontal transformation from the vertical geoid/datum component.
guards: Do not compare GNSS ETRS89 positions directly with OSGB36 National Grid coordinates without transformation.
Do not treat an old archived OSGB36 coordinate as necessarily identical to an OS Net/OSTN15 refix.
Require both horizontal and vertical datum provenance for height-difference acceptance.
Do not label ellipsoidal GNSS height as ODN/Newlyn height without OSGM15 or equivalent documented conversion.
Keep transformation version in the reproducibility record.
Reject mixed-datum candidate samples where the transform chain cannot be reconstructed.
